records.name: Delaware
records.summary: The July 2026 national legal-risk assessment places Delaware in its “low-risk states” group — states that largely refrain from targeting transgender adults without specialising in their protection — and nothing in Delaware’s record rises above that description in either direction. A national equality tracker records no public-facility-use ban for Delaware, and a September 2026 status check likewise found no enacted facility ban, while flagging that the tracker’s own citation (a page since relocated) still awaits one manual re-verification.

sources.summary: July 2026 assessment lists Delaware in its Low-Risk States group (AZ, DE, ME, MI, NV, PA, VA, WI, DC): states that largely refrain from targeting transgender adults without specialising in their protection.

NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (HTTP 404 at the archived URL); the underlying Movement Advancement Project equality map tracks state-by-state bans on transgender people using public bathrooms and facilities according to their gender identity and records no such ban for Delaware.

records.name: Maryland
records.summary:
This state is one of the most legally protective in the country: its health-equity act, effective January 2024, mandates public-insurance coverage of gender-affirming treatment (hormones, puberty blockers and surgery) for an estimated 94,000 trans residents, tens of thousands, with the July 2026 national risk map counting that coverage among the country's most protective.

Protective law has not produced safety: an overlay of national monitoring records several hundred confirmed killings of trans women countrywide since 2008, a conservative undercount, and puts this state among the highest per-capita rates, and in 2026 two Black trans women were fatally shot in this state's largest city ten weeks apart, the most recent in September 2026, with the perpetrator still at large. Visitors should weigh the protections against that violence data.

sources.summary: July 2026 analysis plots recorded anti-trans incidents against each state's law score: Maryland sits in the 'Safest States' band (law score 23.5) with 11.1 recorded incidents, while Louisiana tops both worst-laws (24.7) and recorded (11.6) - the piece's point is that protective law floors do not by themselves predict incident counts.

Report of September 13, 2026: on Friday September 11, 2026 a 27-year-old Black trans woman (Sophie Lee) was found shot in Baltimore's Charles Village and died - the second Black trans woman shot to death in Baltimore within ten weeks.

Firm-blog tracker with May 2024 updates on Maryland's Trans Health Equity Act: the Act passed the Maryland House of Delegates (page dated May 20, 2024, sponsor line Del. Anne Kaiser, D-Montgomery), extending Medicaid coverage of gender-affirming treatment; page follows the measure's path through the Maryland Senate.
